dek_candidates: A price range, not a single number—until demand settles it. Here's how the band works.
Why IPOs show a range instead of a price, and what the limits on that range mean for investors.
design_notes: The intro should lead with the core idea: book-building discovers price from demand. No source needed for that definition.
Each section opens with a plain-language teaching beat before grounding with regulations.
Radical restraint: 6 sections total, no filler. The article will be around 1400 words.
Banned constructions and vocabulary avoided in beats as per anti-slop spec.

beats.beat: Book-building means the company announces a price band, not a fixed price, and lets investor demand over a few days determine the final price. Contrast with fixed-price where a single price is set upfront.
The final price is set after the bidding closes, based on demand, and is filed in the prospectus with the Registrar of Companies.

intro.purpose: Define book-building and contrast with fixed-price issue in plain terms.

beats.beat: An IPO cannot proceed to allotment if the number of successful allottees is less than 1,000.
Allotment for categories other than retail, non-institutional, and anchor investors (i.e., QIBs and employees) must be done on a proportionate basis within the category.

minimum-allottees-allotment.heading: The floor on valid allotment
minimum-allottees-allotment.purpose: Explain that at least 1,000 allottees are required for a valid IPO, and that QIB and employee allotments are on a proportionate basis.

beats.beat: The issuer sets a minimum application value between ₹10,000 and ₹15,000. All applications must be in multiples of that minimum lot.
For a fresh issue, at least 25% of the issue price must be paid at the time of application. For an offer for sale, the full price must be paid upfront.

minimum-application.heading: The minimum you can apply for
minimum-application.purpose: Explain the minimum application value (₹10,000 to ₹15,000), multiples, and the minimum payment required on application (25% for fresh issue, full for offer for sale).

beats.beat: The price band has a floor (lowest price) and a cap (highest). The cap cannot be more than 120% of the floor, and must be at least 105% of the floor.
The floor price or final price cannot be less than the face value of the share (typically ₹1 or ₹10). This sets a minimum.
The issuer must announce the floor price or price band at least two working days before the issue opens, through pre-issue and price band advertisements in newspapers.
The advertisement must include relevant financial ratios for both ends of the band and a note directing investors to the 'basis of issue price' section.

price-band-limits.heading: The price band: what it is and the hard limits on it
price-band-limits.purpose: Explain the price band as a range with a floor price and cap, with the regulatory constraints: cap ≤120% of floor, floor ≥ face value, must be advertised at least 2 working days before issue opens.

beats.beat: An IPO must be open for at least three working days and no more than ten working days.
If the price band is revised during the issue, the bidding period is extended by a minimum of three working days (within the overall 10-day limit).
In case of force majeure or banking strike, the period may be extended by at least one working day, with reasons recorded in writing.

subscription-timeline.heading: How long the IPO stays open
subscription-timeline.purpose: Explain the minimum and maximum subscription period, and what happens if the price band is revised or a force majeure event occurs.

beats.beat: The issuer appoints one or more merchant bankers as lead managers. Their names appear in the offer document.
The lead manager must compulsorily underwrite the issue. If the issue is undersubscribed, the shortfall is made good by the lead manager(s). Syndicate members sub-underwrite with the lead.

underwriting-lead-manager.heading: Who runs the book and underwrites it
underwriting-lead-manager.purpose: Explain the role of the lead manager (merchant banker) and compulsory underwriting.
